title: Pilot evidence composition playbook (draft)
body:
Purpose:
To give sellers a compact, repeatable way to assemble and present micro-evidence during a pilot so that technical and business stakeholders can quickly validate Redwood’s claims on reliability, latency economics, and predictable capacity. This is a working playbook: assume gaps, flag decisions, and iterate.

Audience:
- Seller / SE running pilot conversations with platform / infra teams
- Ops champion at customer responsible for throughput evaluation
- Engagement PM who owns pilot acceptance criteria

What counts as ‘micro-evidence’ (short list):
- Quant snapshots: 95p latency, median latency, tokens/sec, cost-per-1M-tokens (hosted vs dedicated).
- Failure-mode vignette: an incident reproduction (short steps), mitigation path (fallback to smaller variant or region), outcome.
- Observability capture: console chart PNG + explanation pointing at root cause or decision point.
- Config diff: what we changed for the pilot vs default (batching, prefix cache, quant profile) and why.
- Safety/compliance note: KMS/HSM usage, audit-log snippet, or policy applied.

Format we expect sellers to produce (single shared doc per pilot):
- 1-line pilot objective and acceptance criteria (what success looks like)
- 3x micro-evidence cards (one per evidence type above) — each card: 1-sentence headline, 2–3 bullet datapoints, quick takeaway, and one recommended next-step.
- Top-3 risks observed and mitigations attempted
- 1 recommended production configuration (model variant / routing policy / batching) and rationale

Micro-evidence card templates (fill-in):
- Card headline: "Latency-resilience vignette — checkout search (demo)"
  - Data: 95p latency before tuning 420ms -> after batching/kv-cache 120ms
  - Context: 8 concurrent clients, seq_length=512, model=x-1.0-q4
  - Takeaway: auto-batching + prefix-cache reduced per-call tail latency; safe to scale to pilot SLA 200ms at 75% throughput
  - Next step: propose 2-week canary on dedicated pool with 20% reserved capacity

- Card headline: "Cost delta snapshot — embed-heavy ingestion"
  - Data: hosted baseline estimated $2.7 / 1k docs -> deduped + streaming cache $0.95 / 1k docs
  - Context: 1M docs, avg tokens/doc 180, embedding model recommended: embed-medium-1
  - Takeaway: caching + batching saves ~65% in token units; highlight to CFO during pilot review
  - Next step: enable server-side prefix cache in pilot cluster; add cost-heatmap to pilot weekly deck

Seller playbook for assembling evidence (step-by-step):
1) Kickoff: collect acceptance criteria and instrument goals into the pilot doc (owner: SE). Link the Confluence pilot template (see linked artifacts).
2) 24–72 hour smoke: run 3 synthetic scenarios (low, mid, high concurrency) and capture latency histograms + throughput numbers. Save charts to the doc.
3) Produce 3 micro-evidence cards within 5 business days. One MUST address reliability/fallback.
4) Meet with customer ops at day 7: walk through cards, confirm which metric maps to their SLOs. Update acceptance criteria if needed.
5) Optional: if regression or unexpected cost, open JIRA (prefix JIRA-4321 pattern) and include artifact links.

Messaging hooks (short lines sellers can use):
- "We’ll validate your SLOs in real traffic — not synthetic benchmarks — and give a concrete change recommendation before any production cutover."
- "If latency spikes, we’ll show the immediate fallback path (model variant & region) and how it affects cost and accuracy."
- "Pilot configs are small diffs from defaults: batching/cache/quantization — we document each change so your infra team can audit."

A/B evidence presentation variations (for different buyer personas):
- For Platform Engineers: focus on observability artifacts, rollout steps, trace-level root cause, and the rollback play.
- For Product Managers: focus on end-user latency percentiles, quality checks, and cost delta at projected scale.
- For Finance/Procurement: show predictable unit economics and a recommended reserved capacity commit that hits target OPEX.

Acceptance checklist (quick):
- [ ] Pilot doc created and shared with customer Google Drive
- [ ] 3 micro-evidence cards completed
- [ ] Console screenshots + raw CSV attached
- [ ] Identified production config & owner assigned
- [ ] If SLA not met, mitigation JIRA opened

Common pitfalls to call out (seller notes):
- Over-indexing on single synthetic test: prefer 3 scenarios and a small synthetic + real replay of sampled traffic.
- Ignoring cold KV-cache effects: measure warm vs cold startup for first 30 minutes.
- Hiding fallback economics: always show worst-case cost for fallback path so finance is comfortable.

Example short narratives (ready-to-copy into email or slide):
- "During our high-concurrency replay we saw median latency 95ms and 95p at 210ms — by enabling prefix cache we dropped 95p to 130ms; we recommend a small dedicated pool to stabilize tail latency under your peak load."
- "We simulated a region failure and automatically routed to a low-cost model variant; availability remained >99.9% while average token cost rose by 12% — we captured the exact routing policy and config so you can reproduce."

Open questions / TODOs (please edit in-line):
- Which cost metric does the customer prefer? (tokens vs request-level)
- Customer privacy/KMS details to validate for Private deployment checklist
- Who on customer side signs off on production cutover (PM, infra lead, security)?

Next steps (owner assignments):
- Aisha: finalize playbook and add two more sample cards for classification and reranking workloads (due 2025-11-12)
- Marcus: add cost-heatmap template and example script in the pilot-scripts repo (PR #87)
- Riley: create a short seller-facing slide (2 pages) with the Acceptance checklist and three evidence cards for demos

Notes on iterating this doc: treat this as a lightweight canonical artifact for pilots. Sellers will fork and adapt, but ask that a copy of the final pilot doc lives in customer Drive and a pointer is added to the Confluence Pilot Toolkit Index (linked above).

Contact / escalation: SE lead (Riley Thompson), GTM pilot ops (Sofia Delgado). For product/runtime questions ping #runtime-pilot on Slack (link in linked artifacts).
